# Custom reviewers in suites

## What to build
Today a suite ignores custom reviewers: `suite/spawn.ts:38-39` blanks `GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS` for every feature run, and the e2e phase (`suite/e2e.ts` `runE2e`) passes no `reviewers` to `runReviewPhase`, so only the built-in code reviewer and live tester run. This task makes a single-repo suite use the same reviewers file as a run (spec goal **MR-07**):

1. `graph-execution suite` takes `--reviewers <file>`, otherwise reads a non-empty `GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS` (`reviewersFileOf`, `review/reviewers.ts:174`). The file is validated before anything is created (exit 2 with the `ReviewersError` text on a bad file), and every reviewer naming its own provider is checked.
2. The suite copies the file byte for byte to `<suiteDir>/reviewers.json` (`RUN_REVIEWERS_FILE`). Without a file nothing is copied and the built-ins apply, exactly as today.
3. Fresh feature runs are spawned with `--reviewers <suiteDir>/reviewers.json` when the copy exists. The child's env keeps `GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS` set to `""`, so only the copy counts. A resumed feature run (`--resume --run <id>`) gets no `--reviewers`: it reads its own copy in its run dir.
4. The e2e phase runs the copy's enabled reviewers (`readRunReviewers(suiteDir)`, built-ins without a copy), with the providers of reviewers that name their own provider, and reads each reviewer's `repoFile` from the suite's integration worktree (`<suiteDir>/worktrees/integration`) instead of the user's checkout.
5. `suite --resume` uses the copy and refuses `--reviewers` (`--resume takes no --reviewers: the reviewers come from the saved suite`).
6. The suite page draws one e2e node per enabled reviewer of the copy, in file order, between `@e2e-validate` and `@e2e-fixer`, named as on a run page (`reviewerViews` in `ui/store.ts:138`).

Only single-repo suites are in scope. The multi-repo suite (`--project`), its joint phase and the README are later tasks; do not add them here. Keep the existing node ids `@e2e-reviewer` and `@e2e-tester` for the built-ins so existing tests and logs keep working.

## Context: files to read before implementing
- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/reviewers.ts` (lines 1–8, 141–196) — `REVIEWERS_ENV`, `RUN_REVIEWERS_FILE`, `ReviewersError`, `loadReviewersFile`, `enabledReviewers`, `reviewersFileOf`, `readRunReviewers`, `reviewerNode`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/launch/preflight.ts` (lines 96–111, 163–238, 240–243) — how a run validates `--reviewers` (`preflight`, `checkReviewerProviders`) and how `--resume` refuses `--reviewers`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/runner/run.ts` (lines 168–173, 294–297, 520–553) — how a run copies its reviewers file and builds `providers` for reviewers with their own provider before `runReviewPhase`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/spawn.ts` (lines 1–54) — `featureArgs`, `defaultSpawn`, the env blanking at line 38–39.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/orchestrator.ts` (lines 26–47 `SuiteOptions`, 121–144 `validateSuite`, 146–192 `startSuite`, 198–239 `resumeSuite`, 294–322 `start()` in `driveFeatures`).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/e2e.ts` (lines 1–117; `runE2e` at lines 76–117, its `runReviewPhase({...})` call at line 85 has no `reviewers`/`providers`; `reviewFiles` at line 109).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/phase.ts` (lines 43–74 `ReviewPhaseOptions`, 345–381 `reviewRound` builds the context with `repoRoot: opts.repo`).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/context.ts` (lines 10–25 `ReviewerContextOptions`, 61–103 `buildReviewerContext`: repo files are read from `opts.repoRoot`).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/cli.ts` (lines 370–428) — the `suite` command; root options are read with `program.opts<RunOptions>()`; `RunOptions.reviewers` exists (line 54–55).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/server.ts` (lines 98–116, 224–231, 386–398 `/api/suite`).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/web/assets/suitepage.js` (lines 50–82 `loopNodes`, 135–183 `buildModel`, 185–219 `layout`, 364–372 `logSource`, 413–419 `DESCRIBE`, 449–453 e2e rows in `infoOf`).
- `packages/graph-execution/src/ui/store.ts` (lines 134–145) — `reviewerViews(reviewers, custom)`.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/orchestrator-e2e.test.ts` (whole file, 239 lines) — the in-process e2e tests with the `prompts` provider mock; copy its `twoFeatures`/`run` helpers for the regression test.
- `packages/graph-execution/src/review/phase-reviewers.test.ts` (lines 12, 31–47, 87–104) — the `security` reviewer fixture and how its label (`security-r0`), role (`reviewer`) and report are asserted.

## Patterns to follow
- Reviewers file validation, from `launch/preflight.ts:220-231`:
  ```ts
  const file = reviewersFileOf(opts.reviewers, opts.env ?? process.env);
  if (file !== undefined) {
    reviewersFile = path.resolve(opts.cwd, file);
    try {
      reviewers = enabledReviewers(await loadReviewersFile(reviewersFile));
    } catch (err) {
      if (err instanceof ReviewersError) throw new UsageError(err.message);
      throw err;
    }
  }
  ```
- Copy byte for byte, `runner/run.ts:170-172`: `await copyFile(opts.reviewersFile, path.join(ctx.runDir, RUN_REVIEWERS_FILE))`.
- Per-reviewer providers, `runner/run.ts:525-530`:
  ```ts
  const reviewers = await readRunReviewers(ctx.runDir);
  const providers: Record<string, Provider> = {};
  for (const name of new Set(reviewers.flatMap((r) => (r.provider && r.provider !== ctx.provider.name ? [r.provider] : [])))) {
    providers[name] = wrap(await getProvider(name, ctx.repo));
  }
  ```
  In `runE2e` the wrap is the existing `teeOutput(watchIdle(watchLoops(trackProcesses(p, suiteDir), …), …), output)` chain around `env.provider` (`e2e.ts`, in the `runReviewPhase` call): factor it into a local `const wrap = (p: Provider): Provider => teeOutput(watchIdle(watchLoops(trackProcesses(p, suiteDir), …)…), output)` and use it for both.
- Node titles: `reviewerViews(list, custom)` gives `{ id, agent, node, title }` where `node` is `reviewerNode(id)` (`@reviewer` for `code`, `@tester`, `@security`). The suite page's e2e node id is `"@e2e-" + node.slice(1)`: `@e2e-reviewer`, `@e2e-tester`, `@e2e-security`.
- Agent log labels are `reviewerLabel(id, round)` = `<id>-r<round>` (`agents/reviewer.ts:245`), so a reviewer's log prefix on the page is `<id>-r` (today `code-r`, `tester-r`).
- Errors at start are `UsageError` (exit 2, `launch/preflight.ts:28`); the CLI prints `error: <message>`.

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/spawn.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: `featureArgs(f, opts)` takes `opts.reviewers?: string`; when set, append `"--reviewers", opts.reviewers` (before `--no-merge`). In `defaultSpawn` keep `[REVIEWERS_ENV]: ""` in the child env but replace the comment at line 38 with: `// Only the suite's copy counts: it is passed as --reviewers; the env var is blanked so a graph-manager setting cannot override it.`
- **GOTCHA**: do not change the `SpawnFeature` signature in this task.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run typecheck`

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/review/context.ts` and `packages/graph-execution/src/review/phase.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: add `repoFilesDir?: string` to `ReviewerContextOptions` ("where each reviewer's `repoFile` is read; `repoRoot` when omitted") and read the repo files from `opts.repoFilesDir ?? opts.repoRoot` in `buildReviewerContext` (line 70, the `readOptional(path.join(opts.repoRoot, name))` map). Add the same optional `repoFilesDir?: string` to `ReviewPhaseOptions` and pass it through in `reviewRound` (`...(opts.repoFilesDir ? { repoFilesDir: opts.repoFilesDir } : {})` next to `repoRoot: opts.repo`, `review/phase.ts:368`).
- **GOTCHA**: runs do not set it, so their behaviour (repo files read from the user's checkout, uncommitted ones included) is unchanged.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-execution -- review/`

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/orchestrator.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `SuiteOptions` gains `reviewers?: string` (`--reviewers`) and `env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv` (where `GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS` is read; `process.env` when omitted).
  - Add an internal helper `async function suiteReviewersFile(cwd: string, flag: string | undefined, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): Promise<string | undefined>` that resolves `reviewersFileOf(flag, env)` against `cwd`, loads it with `loadReviewersFile` (turning `ReviewersError` into `UsageError`) and returns the absolute path, or `undefined` without a file. A later task (the multi-repo suite) reuses this helper, so keep the name.
  - `validateSuite` (lines 121–144): accept `reviewers`/`env` in its `Pick`, call `suiteReviewersFile` before the per-feature loop, call `checkReviewerProviders(enabledReviewers(await loadReviewersFile(file)), opts.provider, cwdRepo)` once when there is a file, pass `reviewers: reviewersFile` (or nothing) to each feature's `preflight` call (line 138), and return `{ features, names, reviewersFile? }`.
  - `startSuite` (lines 146–192): after the `mkdir` calls (line 159–160), when `reviewersFile` is set: `await copyFile(reviewersFile, path.join(suiteDir, RUN_REVIEWERS_FILE))`.
  - `driveFeatures` `start()` (lines 294–304): for a fresh start, pass `reviewers: path.join(suiteDir, RUN_REVIEWERS_FILE)` to `featureArgs` when `existsSync` of that file; the `--resume` branch stays as it is.
  - `resumeSuite` (lines 198–239): after `SuiteStore.load`, call `await checkReviewerProviders(await readRunReviewers(suiteDir), store.state.provider, repo)` so a missing reviewer CLI fails before restarting anything.
- **IMPORTS**: `copyFile` from `node:fs/promises`; `checkReviewerProviders` from `../launch/preflight.js`; `enabledReviewers`, `loadReviewersFile`, `readRunReviewers`, `reviewersFileOf`, `ReviewersError`, `RUN_REVIEWERS_FILE` from `../review/reviewers.js`.
- **GOTCHA**: the child's `preflight` must not see the parent's env var: the spawn already blanks it, and `validateSuite` passes the resolved file explicitly so a file given only through the env var is still validated per feature.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run typecheck`

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/e2e.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: in `runE2e`, `const reviewers = await readRunReviewers(suiteDir);`, build `providers` for reviewers whose `provider` differs from `state.provider` with `getProvider(name, ctx.repo)` and the same wrap chain as the main provider, then pass `reviewers`, `providers` and `repoFilesDir: integrationWorktreeOf(suiteDir)` to `runReviewPhase`.
- **IMPORTS**: `getProvider` from `../providers/index.js`; `type Provider` from `../providers/types.js`; `readRunReviewers` from `../review/reviewers.js`.
- **GOTCHA**: `reviewFiles: await overlapFiles(ctx)` applies to every `diff` reviewer (`review/phase.ts:416-438`): a custom diff reviewer only reviews files changed by 2+ features, and writes "<name> not needed" otherwise. Keep that.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-execution -- suite/orchestrator-e2e`

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/cli.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: in the `suite` command (line 371 on), add `.option("--reviewers <file>", "reviewers file (JSON) for the feature runs and the e2e phase; default: $GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS, else the built-in code reviewer and live tester")`. Read it as `opts.reviewers ?? root.reviewers` (the root command declares `--reviewers` too and may take it). With `--resume`, throw `new UsageError("--resume takes no --reviewers: the reviewers come from the saved suite")` next to the `--feature` check (line 388). Put `reviewers` into `suiteOpts` (line 401–409) so `runSuite`, `serveSuite` and the `--web` check (`validateSuite`, line 416–418) all see it.
- **GOTCHA**: `--web` re-runs the same argv in a detached `--web-serve` child (`launchWeb`), so the flag is passed through without extra work; the env var is inherited.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run build -w graph-execution && node packages/graph-execution/dist/cli.js suite --help` shows `--reviewers`.

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/server.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: `/api/suite` (lines 386–398, the response at line 397) also returns `reviewers: reviewerViews(list, custom)` and `customReviewers: custom`, where `list = await readRunReviewers(suiteDir)` (catch → `BUILTIN_REVIEWERS`) and `custom = existsSync(path.join(suiteDir, RUN_REVIEWERS_FILE))`. Read them once per server (the copy never changes) into a lazily created promise.
- **IMPORTS**: `reviewerViews` from `../ui/store.js`; `BUILTIN_REVIEWERS`, `readRunReviewers`, `RUN_REVIEWERS_FILE` from `../review/reviewers.js`; `existsSync` from `node:fs`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-execution -- suite/server`

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/web/assets/suitepage.js`
- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `loopNodes(r, ready, failed, fixers, ids)` takes the reviewer ids (default `["code", "tester"]`) and returns `reviewers: { [id]: node }` built with the existing `reviewed(r.reports[id])`; keep `nodes.reviewer`/`nodes.tester` filled for the feature boxes (they still draw only the code reviewer and tester: feature boxes are not in scope).
  - In `buildModel` (lines 172–181) replace the fixed `@e2e-reviewer`/`@e2e-tester` nodes by one node per `d.reviewers` entry (fallback to code + tester when absent), id `"@e2e-" + r.node.slice(1)`, parent `@e2e-validate`. Title: `r.title` when `d.customReviewers`, else the historic titles (`cross-feature review` for `code`, `e2e tester` for `tester`). `@e2e-fixer`'s parents are all those nodes (or `@e2e-validate` when no reviewer is enabled).
  - In `layout` (line 214) the second e2e row is the list of those node ids.
  - `logSource` (line 370): for an `@e2e-<x>` reviewer node use prefix `<id>-r` (look the id up from the model node, e.g. store `reviewerId` on it); keep `@e2e-fixer` → `fix`.
  - `infoOf` (lines 449–453): for a custom reviewer node show `"<name>: reviews the files several features changed, with every PRD."`.
- **GOTCHA**: this is plain browser JS served from `web/assets/` (no build step); keep it ES2020 and in the file's style.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run lint`

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/orchestrator-e2e.test.ts` (regression tests)
- **IMPLEMENT**: in `describe("suite e2e phase and apply")`, add `it("runs the reviewers file in every feature run and in the e2e phase")`: write `{ reviewers: [code, tester, security] }` (copy the shapes from `review/phase-reviewers.test.ts:12`, `security = { id: "security", type: "diff", name: "Security", repoFile: "SECURITY_REVIEW.md" }`) to `<repo>/.git/reviewers.json`, commit a `SECURITY_REVIEW.md` holding `Check the secrets.` in the repo, use `twoFeatures(repo, { overlap: true })`, and run `runSuite({ …, reviewers: file })` (extend the local `run` helper with an optional `reviewers`). Assert: exit 0 and `applied`; `<suiteDir>/reviewers.json` has the same bytes as the source; for each feature `<suiteDir>/features/<runId>/reviewers.json` exists and `<suiteDir>/features/<runId>/reports/round0/security.json` exists; `prompts` has a `reviewer:security-r0` entry whose prompt contains `Check the secrets.`; `<suiteDir>/reports/round0/security.json` exists.
  Add `it("reads GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS when --reviewers is not given")` with `vi.stubEnv("GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS", file)` (and `vi.unstubAllEnvs()` in `finally`): `<suiteDir>/reviewers.json` exists. In the existing test "records the code review as not needed when no file overlaps" add `expect(existsSync(path.join(dir, "reviewers.json"))).toBe(false)`.
- **PATTERN**: `suite/orchestrator-e2e.test.ts:175-195` (the overlap test and its `run` helper that swaps in the in-process script after the features end).
- **GOTCHA**: the feature runs are child processes; their `security-r0` reviewer runs with the fake provider's default (a valid empty report) unless scripted. The in-process e2e script needs `suiteTester` and `suiteExtra` as in the existing overlap test.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-execution -- suite/orchestrator-e2e`

### UPDATE `packages/graph-execution/src/suite/server.test.ts` and `packages/graph-execution/src/cli.test.ts`
- **IMPLEMENT**: server: a test that `/api/suite` returns `reviewers` with ids `["code", "tester"]` and `customReviewers: false` for the `setup()` folder, and the names of a `reviewers.json` written into the suite dir before `setup` returns (write it, then fetch) with `customReviewers: true`. CLI: `it("exits 2 for an invalid suite --reviewers file, before creating a suite")` running `suite --feature a:PRD-a.md --feature b:PRD-b.md --provider fake --reviewers nope.json` in a temp repo (copy `cli.test.ts:120-127`): exit 2, stderr contains `reviewers file not found`, no `.graph-execution` folder. And `suite --resume --reviewers x.json` exits 2 with `--resume takes no --reviewers`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm test -w graph-execution -- suite/server cli`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `suite --reviewers <file>` with a reviewer `security` runs `security` in each feature run (its report is in each feature run's `reports/round0/security.json`) and in the e2e phase (`<suiteDir>/reports/round0/security.json`); `<suiteDir>/reviewers.json` is a byte copy of the file.
- [ ] Without `--reviewers` and without `GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS`, no `reviewers.json` is written and the suite behaves as today (code reviewer and tester); every existing suite test still passes.
- [ ] A non-empty `GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS` is used when `--reviewers` is absent; the feature runs still see an empty env var and get `--reviewers <suiteDir>/reviewers.json`.
- [ ] An invalid or missing reviewers file exits 2 before any suite folder exists; `suite --resume --reviewers x` exits 2.
- [ ] The e2e reviewers read their `repoFile` from `<suiteDir>/worktrees/integration`.
- [ ] `/api/suite` returns `reviewers` and `customReviewers`; the suite page shows one e2e node per enabled reviewer (a `Security` node with a custom file), and its Logs tab shows `security-r<n>` logs.
- [ ] The regression tests above exist and pass.

## Validation commands
```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-execution -- suite/ review/ cli
```
